oewn-01867145-a.learner: not private, but open to everyone or having to do with all the people.
examples: I cannot see that London has any great advantage over the country, for my part, except the shops and public places.
private balls are much pleasanter than public ones

oewn-00495342-s.learner: having an effect on all the people of a place.
examples: The new tax on bread was a matter of public concern.

oewn-06645870-n.learner: words that say you are sorry for having caused someone trouble.
examples: Mrs. Bennet began repeating her thanks to Mr. Bingley for his kindness to Jane, with an apology for troubling him also with Lizzy.
Mr. Collins repeated his apologies in quitting the room

oewn-05829462-n.learner: a poor example of the thing it is meant to be.
examples: The cold soup and dry bread were an apology for a dinner.

connotation.why: names the thing by how badly it falls short

oewn-06753614-n.learner: a formal piece of writing that defends something you believe in strongly.
examples: He wrote a long apology for the beliefs of his church.
Caroline boasted joyfully of their increasing intimacy
I am astonished at his intimacy with Mr. Bingley.

oewn-07545512-n.learner: the feeling of being close to someone and of belonging together.
examples: Sitting by the fire without speaking, they felt a quiet intimacy.

oewn-13954922-n.learner: a sexual relationship, usually one kept secret or not allowed.
examples: Their intimacy was discovered, and both families were disgraced.

connotation.why: casts the relationship as secret and improper

oewn-00687584-v.learner: to not take something that is given or offered to you.
examples: If, therefore, she actually persists in rejecting my suit, perhaps it were better not to force her into accepting me
Mr. Hurst soon found even his open petition rejected.

oewn-02242120-v.learner: to not accept that something is true.
examples: if you do not absolutely reject it as false, you will, I hope, acquit me henceforth of cruelty towards Mr. Wickham

oewn-00687320-v.learner: to drop someone or something from what is being considered, or from a contest.
examples: without knowing or considering what their income might be, rejected many as deficient in size and importance

oewn-06751030-n.learner: something said or written that makes a thing easy to understand by telling how it is built, how it works, or what the situation was.
examples: Mr. Darcy's explanation there had appeared very insufficient; and she read it again.

oewn-07247081-n.learner: the act of explaining, that is, making something clear.
examples: Miss Bingley persevered, therefore, in requiring an explanation of his two motives.
she wrote a short letter to her aunt, to request an explanation of what Lydia had dropped

oewn-05801008-n.learner: an idea in your mind that makes something make sense.
examples: The only explanation she could think of was that he had lost his way.

oewn-00053917-n.learner: the act of going away in a polite way.
examples: Elizabeth took leave of the whole party in the liveliest spirits.
She asked leave to speak before the others began.

oewn-15164090-n.learner: the stretch of time in which you are away from your work or duty.
examples: The officer came home on leave for a fortnight.

oewn-00894444-v.learner: to admit that you have done wrong or fallen short.
examples: if my manner has been at all reprehensible, I here beg leave to apologize
Be so kind as to apologize for us to Miss Darcy.

oewn-00896259-v.learner: to give reasons that defend something, explain it, clear it away, or excuse it.
examples: Later writers apologized for the poet's harshness by pointing to the age he lived in.

oewn-03410635-n.learner: the things put into a room or other space to make it ready for people to live or work in.
examples: The hall, the dining-room, and all its furniture, were examined and praised
She related the dimensions of the rooms, and the price of the furniture in vain.

oewn-01559703-v.learner: to force, take, or pull things apart from each other.
examples: I did everything in my power to separate my friend from your sister

oewn-02627934-v.learner: to lie between two things like a barrier.
examples: The garden in which stands my humble abode is separated only by a lane from Rosings Park.

oewn-02034003-v.learner: to move apart and go your own way.
examples: They had not long separated when Miss Bingley came towards her.
When they left the high road for the lane to Hunsford, every eye was in search of the Parsonage.
she turned up the lane which led her farther from the turnpike road

oewn-03645974-n.learner: a marked strip of a track or road, such as one for a swimmer or for one line of cars.
examples: The swimmer in the outside lane touched the wall first.
